caption: Paul directly connects Deuteronomy’s curse with Jesus on the cross. It is powerful Christian typology—but the original burial law does not forecast Jesus.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did this curse predict the cross? Deuteronomy calls a body hung on wood cursed by God. Paul says Jesus became a curse for others by hanging on a cross.
slides.body: Deuteronomy calls a body hung on wood cursed by God. Paul says Jesus became a curse for others by hanging on a cross.
slides.heading: Did this curse predict the cross?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Deut 21:23: anyone who is hung on a tree is under God’s curse.
slides.body: anyone who is hung on a tree is under God’s curse.
slides.heading: Deut 21:23

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Gal 3:13, BSB: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
slides.body: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Gal 3:13

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Paul makes the connection He quotes Deuteronomy directly and uses it to explain how Jesus redeems people from the law’s curse.
slides.body: He quotes Deuteronomy directly and uses it to explain how Jesus redeems people from the law’s curse.
slides.heading: Paul makes the connection

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the law does not forecast Jesus Deuteronomy orders burial of an executed criminal’s displayed body. Paul later applies that old rule to the cross.
slides.body: Deuteronomy orders burial of an executed criminal’s displayed body. Paul later applies that old rule to the cross.
slides.heading: But the law does not forecast Jesus

title: Cursed on a tree
